title.narrative: Strengthening Community Economic Resilience (SCER) through Inclusive, Innovative, and Climate-Smart Nutrition Sensitive Food System Interventions

description.narrative: ltpgtThe 3rd Lean Season Allocation adopts a comprehensive approach to enhance disability inclusion, protection, participation, and access for people with disabilities (PWDs) and other vulnerable groups facing food security, nutrition and protection risks in Jere (Borno) and Madagali (Adamawa).ltbrgtBuilding on CDHI’s previous climate-smart agriculture initiatives implemented in collaboration with CAID and WFP, this project supports the sustainability of NHF-backed programs and complements the Second Lean Season Allocation, ensuring continuity and scalability of protection and food security outcomes.ltbrgtCDHI will facilitate the Strengthening of Community Economic Resilience (SCER) through Inclusive, Innovative, and Climate-Smart Nutrition Sensitive Food System Interventions in Jere LGA of Borno state. The planned intervention will leverage on CDHIs experiences and community presence in the implementation of climate smart nutrition sensitive food systems resilience interventions. ltbrgtThe proposed project ensures disability inclusion is at the center of the food security response. Food insecure HHs will be targeted for food assistance using climate smart agricultural practices. The targeting approach will ensure that disability related indicators are considered as a key entry point. Specifically, CDHI will implement the following activities.ltbrgt Implementing inclusive, innovative, and climate-smart nutrition interventions in Jere LGA, leveraging CDHI’s community experience.ltbrgt Prioritizing disability inclusion in food security responses, with targeted support for food-insecure households using climate-smart agricultural practices.ltbrgt Introducing hydroponics and other climate-smart methods to address land and water scarcity, enabling year-round production of green fodder for livestock.ltbrgt Distributing improved seedlings, hydroponic kits, animal ruminants, farm inputs, and backyard gardening kits to 250 households, focusing on those with disabilities.ltbrgt Promoting social cohesion and mitigating community tensions through participatory planning and inclusive targeting.ltbrgt Facilitating community-based participatory planning (CBPP) to establish early warning systems and implement cash-for-work initiatives to address identified risks.ltbrgt Supporting backyard gardening at the community level to improve household nutrition.ltbrgt Providing capacity-building initiatives to strengthen resilience at both household and community levels.ltbrgt Collaborating with governance structures to deliver cash transfers and strengthen SOCU’s capacity to include disability indicators in food security related CBT targeting.ltbrgtThis project places disability inclusion at the center of food security interventions, aiming to build resilient, nutrition-sensitive food systems and sustainable livelihoods for the most vulnerable populations.ltbrgt lt/pgt
